# Open Software Factory

> Open Software Factory is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) Claude Code plugin that gives you a team of AI agents (Team Lead, Architect, Developer, Tester, Security and more) to take your spec to a tested, reviewed release, and it stops for your approval before any push, merge or deploy.

## Install

Paste this line into a terminal once per machine:

```
claude plugin marketplace add achisolomon/open-software-factory && claude plugin install software-factory@software-factory-marketplace --scope user
```

## The 7 steps

- Step one: You hand over a spec, written with the spec tool you like. The Product Manager checks it for gaps and never rewrites it.
- Step two: The Team Lead classifies every request first: its type, its size and the reviewers it needs. Small work takes the fast path.
- Step three: The Architect splits the design into small tasks. A Developer builds one task at a time, with unit tests, and the Test Engineer hunts for where it breaks.
- Step four: Every task is reviewed. The Architect checks the code; Security, FinOps and UX can join. A finding goes back to the Developer, for at most three fix rounds.
- Step five: Independent tasks can run side by side when you choose speed. The Team Lead posts a status board: who is running, blocked, done, and what is next.
- Step six: The Team Lead stops at three gates: the requirements, the design with its cost, and the release. Nothing moves on until you approve.
- Step seven: No push, merge, deploy, paid resource or data deletion happens without your explicit approval. The Team Lead holds the release until you say yes.

## Agents

<!-- roster:start -->
- Team Lead (Your session's model (Opus by default)): Runs the process: plans the work, hands it to the right specialist, keeps the status board, holds the gates and talks to you.
- Triage Classifier (Haiku): Sorts every new request first, so small work takes the fast path and big work gets the full process. Read-only.
- Product Manager (Opus): Turns your idea or spec into a clear PRD and a backlog of stories with testable acceptance criteria, and checks your spec for gaps.
- Project Manager (Haiku): Keeps the GitHub issues and the project board current as work moves, and audits the board before each gate.
- Software Architect (Opus): Designs the system, writes the decisions and contracts, breaks the work into tasks and reviews the code.
- Software Developer (Sonnet): Builds one task at a time with unit tests on a local branch, and fixes what the reviewers find.
- Test Automation Engineer (Sonnet): The devil's advocate: plans the tests, writes integration and end-to-end tests, and hunts for where the code breaks.
- Exploratory QA Engineer (Sonnet): Explores the running app like a user, in local or disposable setups only, and turns each bug into a failing repro test.
- DevOps Engineer (Sonnet): Sets up environments, containers, CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and checks them with dry runs.
- FinOps Engineer (Sonnet): Models the cost with sourced prices, sets cost guardrails and reviews changes for what they will cost.
- Security Engineer (Opus): Threat-models the design, sets the security requirements, reviews and scans the code, and holds the final release gate.
- UX/UI Designer (Sonnet): Designs user flows and screens, and reviews UI changes for usability and accessibility.
- Performance Engineer (Opus): Load-tests the system and finds what breaks under load, before a merge to main or a deploy.
- Retro (Sonnet): Once a day, reads how the sessions went and drafts small fixes for the causes. They wait for your yes.
- Your agent (Your choice): Add your own specialist as one agent file. Open a discussion on the repo to share the idea.
<!-- roster:end -->

## Safety and cost

- No push to a shared branch, merge to main, deploy, paid resource or data deletion happens without your explicit approval of that specific action. The trust model is in TRUST.md: https://github.com/achisolomon/open-software-factory/blob/main/docs/TRUST.md
- Each agent runs on the smallest model that does its job well. Say "conserve my limits" to go cheaper; that changes models, never steps or gates.
- The code the agents write in your own project is yours. The license covers the factory itself.

## Works with

- Claude Code, in a terminal or in the VS Code extension.
